commitResults.messageTitle: Match student names ignoring case and spacing
commitResults.messageBody:
Treat names that differ only in letter case or whitespace as the same
student, so that adding 'john tan' when 'John Tan' exists is rejected as
a duplicate. Real-world names are not case-sensitive, and the PE bug
guidelines treat case-sensitive duplicate detection as a feature flaw.

Add Name#isSameName and use it in Student#isSameStudent.

they were given in, and the same subject given twice (ignoring case)
is rejected. Subjects are not yet stored in Student; a later PR will
replace tags with subjects.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate student names using the feature spec rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Follow the F1 rules in the Week 6 feature spec: names are 1 to 50
characters, contain at least one letter, and use only letters
(including accented and non-Latin letters), spaces, hyphens,
apostrophes or full stops. This accepts names such as O'Brien,
Mary-Anne and José, which AB3 rejected, and rejects digits.

Repeated spaces between words are reduced to one when parsing, so
'John   Tan' is stored as 'John Tan' instead of being rejected.

Add 'student view n/NAME' (F2), which shows a student's name and
subjects, or '(none recorded)' if there are none. The name is matched
ignoring case and extra spaces through Model#findStudentByName, and an
unknown name gives "No student named '<name>' found."

The command only reads data; it does not change the student list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use feature spec messages for student add and view
commitResults.messageBody:
Match the F1 and F2 outputs in the Week 6 feature spec:

* student add shows '✔ Student added: NAME (subjects: ...)' or
  '(no subjects recorded)', followed by the total number of students.
* A duplicate name gives "A student named 'NAME' already exists.
  Student names must be unique."
* Format errors for student add and student view show the command
  format, e.g. 'Command format: student add n/NAME [s/SUBJECT]...'.

Every error shown in the result display now starts with ❌, so all
commands, including later interaction and follow-up commands, follow
the team's message rule without extra code.

commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Normalize student names to Unicode NFC
commitResults.messageBody:
A composed "é" and an "e" followed by a combining accent look the
same but compared as different names, so TutorLink could hold two
visually identical students.

Store every Name in NFC form and check the length limit on that
form. Lookup, duplicate detection, display and the data file then
all use one spelling, and two such names in a saved file are
rejected as duplicates on load. find also composes its keywords.

commitResults.messageTitle: Turn pasted line breaks into spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX TextField drops line breaks, so pasting "line one" and
"line two" on separate lines joined them into "line oneline two"
without any message. Replace each line break with a space before
the text reaches the command box, and say so in the UG instead of
the single-line error that could never appear in the app.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn and back up when the data file is unreadable
commitResults.messageBody:
An invalid data file made TutorLink start with no students and no
message, and the next change overwrote the file, losing the data.

Copy the unreadable file to tutorlink.json.bak before anything can
overwrite it, and show a warning naming the backup in the result
box. If the copy fails, the warning says so instead. Update the UG
caution to describe this and how to recover.
